gaps.sentence: In your position, I ___ for a written contract.
gaps.explanation: Giving imaginary advice uses 'would' for an unreal present: would ask.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ late again, the manager will have to speak to you.
gaps.hint: a warning about a real future
gaps.explanation: A real warning about the future keeps the if-clause in the present simple: are.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ to your advice — then I would not be in this mess.
gaps.hint: regret about the past, past perfect
gaps.explanation: 'Wish' plus the past perfect expresses regret about the past: had listened.

gaps.sentence: Had I ___ the risks, I would never have invested.
gaps.explanation: After inverted 'Had I', the past participle follows: known.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ how to play the piano.
gaps.hint: wish plus past for present regret
gaps.explanation: 'Wish' plus past simple expresses regret about a present situation: knew.

gaps.sentence: If she were more organised, she ___ the deadline last week.
gaps.explanation: A present unreal cause with a past result is a mixed conditional: would not have missed.

gaps.sentence: Unless something urgent ___, I will be at my desk all morning.
gaps.hint: unless introduces the exception, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' introduces the exception to the plan and takes the present simple: comes up.

gaps.sentence: You will not pass the course unless you ___ all the assignments.
gaps.hint: unless means if not, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' introduces a negative condition and takes the present simple: complete.
